sections.h2: What does the Grand Traverse County Register of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds is the recording office for land records in Grand Traverse County: deeds, mortgages, land contracts, liens and related papers. Records are open to the public. The computer image index reaches back to 1966, and older documents, some from 1853, can be pulled by liber and page.

The office does not hand out blank deeds or advise on how to draft one. The county's own page suggests an attorney who knows Michigan real property law, a local title company, or a completed blank deed that meets recording rules, and it warns that forms found online may not conform.

The county seat is Traverse City. Grand Traverse County covers 601 square miles, of which 23% is water, and it is named for Grand Traverse Bay. It was first created in 1840 as Omeena County and reorganized under its present name in 1851, after the 1839 mission at Old Mission established the first permanent settlement. The Census Bureau counts 96,729 residents in its 2025 estimate, making it the most populous county in Northern Michigan.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Grand Traverse County?
sections.html:
The recording fee is $30.00 for a deed, mortgage, lis pendens, certified copy or other instrument, however many pages it runs. Checks are made payable to Register of Deeds or GTROD, and mailed submissions need a self addressed stamped envelope or $3.00 for postage and handling.

Grand Traverse County recording charges listed by the Register of Deeds
ItemCharge
Deed, mortgage or other instrument$30.00 per document
Extra instrument assigned or discharged$3 each
Tax certification on a warranty deed$5 per deed, up to 25 parcels, then $0.20 per added parcel
Copies in the office$1.00 per page, plus $5.00 if certified
County transfer tax$1.10 per $1,000 in $500 steps
State transfer tax$7.50 per $1,000 in $500 steps

The statutory fee schedule is set in MCL 600.2567. The county's fee page was last stamped effective October 1, 2016, so confirm the figures with the office before sending a check.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax figured in Grand Traverse County?
sections.html:
Any deed or easement with consideration owes state and county transfer tax when it is recorded, unless an exemption is stated on the instrument. The tax runs on the sale price rounded up to the next $500.

  • County rate: 55 cents per $500 under MCL 207.504 for a county of this size, which the county page expresses as $1.10 per $1,000.
  • State rate: $3.75 per $500 under MCL 207.525, shown on the county page as $7.50 per $1,000.
  • Combined, that is $8.60 per $1,000 of rounded value.

The county's example takes a $110,100 price, rounds it to $110,500, and arrives at $950.30 in total, made up of $828.75 state tax and $121.55 county tax. A $110,501 price rounds to $111,000 and costs $954.60. The instrument must show the full value on its face, or an affidavit stating the value must be attached.

Exemptions are listed in MCL 207.505 for the county tax and MCL 207.526 for the state tax. They include transfers for under $100, deeds given in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure, conveyances from a parent to a child or grandchild, court-ordered transfers without stated consideration, and quitclaim deeds that only correct a flaw in title.

sections.h2: Who certifies taxes before a deed is recorded in Grand Traverse County?
sections.html:
The County Treasurer does. Under MCL 211.135, a warranty deed, land contract, or any deed with a covenant of warranty needs treasurer certificates showing no tax liens and that taxes were paid for the five years before the instrument. The register will not record it without them, and a quitclaim deed with no covenant of warranty is excepted.

The treasurer's office is at 400 Boardman Avenue, Suite 104, Traverse City, and takes calls at 231-922-4735. Request the certification before the closing date so the recorded deed does not wait on it.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid property tax in Grand Traverse County?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes become delinquent on March 1 of the year after they were billed, and payment moves from the township or city treasurer to the County Treasurer. Between July 1 and the end of February, current bills go to the local treasurer.

The county adds a 4% administration fee and interest of 1% per month. After one year the property is forfeited, interest rises to 1.5% per month retroactive to the delinquency date, and a $175 title search fee and notice fees are added. Another year later, on March 31, the property is foreclosed. The county says foreclosure is final and the owner cannot get the property back.

  • Partial payments are accepted and reduce the interest that keeps building.
  • At least five notices go out: two by first class mail, two by certified mail, and one by personal service.
  • An owner who loses a property that sells for more than the debt must file a Notice of Claim by July 1 and then a court motion for the surplus.

The Treasurer's FAQ also warns that a mortgage company can miss a payment, especially after a refinance, and that Michigan law still holds the owner responsible.

sections.h2: What are the Grand Traverse County housing numbers?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates put the median value of an owner-occupied home in the county at $339,400, and 77.2% of housing units are owner-occupied. Median household income is $81,647, median gross rent is $1,288, and 25.1% of residents are 65 or older. The county has 40,287 households and about 464 square miles of land.

Those figures are a reminder that a Grand Traverse County deed often carries a large transfer tax. At the county's combined rate, a $339,400 sale would be rounded to $339,500 and cost about $2,919.70 to record with state and county tax.

Anyone selling a house that has tenants, repairs, or back taxes should line up the treasurer's certification and a payoff letter early, then give the title company a clean copy of the deed to the register.

faqs.q: How much does the Grand Traverse County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: $30.00 per document regardless of page count, plus transfer tax when there is a sale price. A warranty deed also needs a $5 tax certification from the County Treasurer.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a home sale in Grand Traverse County?
faqs.a: $8.60 per $1,000 of value rounded up to the next $500, split into $7.50 state and $1.10 county. A $110,500 price, for example, owes $950.30.

faqs.q: Does Grand Traverse County accept electronic recording?
faqs.a: The county's own fee page does not describe e-recording, so ask the Register of Deeds before relying on it. Mailed documents need a return envelope or $3.00 for postage and handling.

faqs.q: When do unpaid taxes go to the Grand Traverse County Treasurer?
faqs.a: On March 1 of the year after they were billed. From then on the county adds a 4% fee and 1% monthly interest, and forfeiture follows a year later.

faqs.q: Does the Register of Deeds prepare deeds in Grand Traverse County?
faqs.a: No. The office supplies no blank deeds and gives no advice on preparing them, so use an attorney or title company.
